rows.note: This is the all-purpose comparative pattern for doing something less skillfully than B.

example.english: I speak English worse than Ming.
example.traditional: 我講英文講得差過阿明。
example.jyutping: ngo5 gong2 jing1 man4 gong2 dak1 caa1 gwo3 aa3 ming4

rows.traditional: V + A + 仲 + ADJ + 過 + B
rows.jyutping: V A zung6 ADJ gwo3 B
rows.note: Use this when the worse effect on A is expressed with a severity adjective such as 大, 重, or 嚴重.

example.english: Handling it this way made the situation worse than before.
example.traditional: 佢咁樣處理，令件事仲嚴重過之前。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam2 joeng2 cyu2 lei5 ling6 gin6 si6 zung6 jim4 zung6 gwo3 zi1 cin4

rows.note: Use this as a colloquial sentence opener meaning “worse still” before introducing an additional problem.

example.english: Worse still, the air conditioner broke down too.
example.traditional: 仲衰嘅係，部冷氣又壞埋。
example.jyutping: zung6 seoi1 ge3 hai6 bou6 laang5 hei3 jau6 waai6 maai4
